sense: to do with religion and worship

terms.grammar: rēs, reī f., with dīvīnus; also singular, rēs dīvīna, a service or sacrifice
terms.comment: Religious, as against secular, business: the plural for religious matters in general, the singular rēs dīvīna for an act of worship (Lewis & Short: “very freq.” in Plautus and Terence). With other nouns Latin usually says sacer.

terms.gloss: sacred, holy; dedicated to God (the gods)
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.129: pūblicīs prīvātīs sacrīs profānīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Consecrated to the divine, as against profānus, not consecrated (Lewis & Short); so a religious building is aedificium sacrum. As a noun, sacra are rites and sacred things.

phrases.latin: aedificiīs omnibus, pūblicīs prīvātīs sacrīs profānīs, sīc pepercit
phrases.english: he spared all the buildings, public and private, religious and secular alike

phrases.latin: illī rēbus dīvīnīs intersunt, sacrificia pūblica ac prīvāta prōcūrant, religiōnēs interpretantur
phrases.english: they take part in worship, look after the sacrifices of the state and of private people, and interpret religious questions

sources: Lewis & Short: divinus · Lewis & Short: sacer
Caesar (BG 6.13.4) quoted as in the record national.
